messages:
eva-ml: Quick share from last night's weight-only INT8 comparison (bitsandbytes vs llm.int8). Bench: kestrel-14b summarization (news_summ_1k), eval-harness v2. High level: bnb gives better throughput but shows a growing quality gap on longform (>256 tokens). llm.int8 keeps ROUGE closer to fp16 but at a throughput/latency cost. Thoughts?

mike-ops: Can you paste the exact commands + runtime config you used so infra can repro perf numbers?

eva-ml: Sure — ran both on the same dedicated pool (4xA100-40GB). Commands:
```bash
run_eval \  
  --model kestrel-14b \  
  --quant weight-only \  
  --backend bnb \  
  --batch 8 \  
  --max-tokens 512 \  
  --temp 0.0 \  
  --promptset news_summ_1k 

# and for llm.int8
run_eval --model kestrel-14b --quant weight-only --backend llm.int8 --batch 4 --max-tokens 512 --temp 0.0 --promptset news_summ_1k
```

jen-qa: What were the metric deltas (ROUGE / ppl / tok/s / latencies)?

eva-ml: Summary table (baseline = fp16):
- fp16 baseline: ROUGE-L 30.3, PPL 12.1, tok/s 720, p50=50ms, p95=150ms
- bitsandbytes (bnb, weight-only): ROUGE-L 27.1, PPL 15.2, tok/s 680, p50=55ms, p95=180ms
- llm.int8 (weight-only): ROUGE-L 29.8, PPL 13.8, tok/s 420, p50=85ms, p95=240ms

Notes: ROUGE measured on greedy decoding to remove sampling variance. The bnb drop is most pronounced on longer summaries (>256 tokens). For short summaries (<128 tokens) bnb is within ~0.9 ROUGE-L of baseline.

kevin-ml: Curious if this is activation scaling / KV cache accumulation. Did you try deterministic beams or different seeds?

eva-ml: Yes — ran greedy (deterministic) and beam=4; the ROUGE gap persists in greedy which points to quantization error rather than sampling. Also ran few runs with different seeds; variance <0.2 ROUGE so not seed-related.

jen-qa: Did you try AWQ or GPTQ variants for reference?

eva-ml: Quick notes: AWQ produced similar end-quality to llm.int8 but had a transient memory spike on warmup that killed 1 host in the pool (investigating). GPTQ-style full quant (per-channel) wasn't tested here (we wanted a weight-only parity comparison).

mike-ops: For rollout: can we route longform requests to fp16 fallback or to llm.int8? Also want a canary before 100% switch.

eva-ml: Proposed rollout config (route by predicted out_tokens):
```json
{
  "name": "weight_only_canary",
  "traffic_split": [{"variant":"bnb-int8","pct":5},{"variant":"llm-int8","pct":5},{"variant":"fp16","pct":90}],
  "routing": [{"predicate":"predicted_out_tokens > 256","fallback":"fp16"}],
  "slo_checks": {"metric":"rouge_l","window":"5m","threshold_drop":1.5}
}
```

deploy-bot: Canary started on dedicated/pool-14b at 2025-11-05T14:32:10Z :rocket:

kevin-ml: Add an eval hook that computes ROUGE-L on the production promptset every 5 minutes. If drop > 1.5 for 5 consecutive windows, auto-roll back canary. Also log token-level attention norm deltas for debugging.

eva-ml: Added notes to the eval artifact location: /mnt/evals/int8/kestrel/1739993337/ — contains per-sample diffs, attention norm traces, and latency histograms. Observed attention-norm drift accumulating after ~120 tokens on bnb runs.

mike-ops: I'll wire the rollback alert and update the canary policy. Thanks for the writeup. :thumbsup:

jen-qa: One more thing — let's add a short regression eval that specifically targets factuality and hallucination slices for longform. If quantization is perturbing logits distribution, we might see factuality regressions even if ROUGE looks OK.

eva-ml: Agreed. I'll add the hallucination slice to the harness and re-run nightly. Will post a follow-up thread with the per-slice results. :eyes:
